findings.title: Default (null-strategy) test case never enables the rolling-updates feature in the CR
findings.body: `createInitialDeployment` returns early when `updateStrategy == null`, so the `rolling-updates` feature is only added to the Keycloak CR for the RECREATE case. The new docs say the feature must be enabled on the CR ("Otherwise, the Operator will fail") and show `<not set>` together with `features.enabled: rolling-updates`. The null case passes only because `Dockerfile-custom-image` now bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the image at build time. The tests therefore never exercise the documented configuration for the default strategy, and a missing or disabled feature in the CR is never tested. Enable the feature for both parameterized cases, or add a case that covers the feature being absent.

findings.title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already configured on the test CR
findings.body: `getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES))` replaces the whole enabled-features list. If `getTestKeycloakDeployment` or a future change already sets enabled features on the FeatureSpec, they are silently dropped. Append to the existing list, or build a mutable list that merges the new key in.

findings.title: New exit codes (4 = feature disabled, 3 = recreate) are not asserted
findings.body: The PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. These are documented as the scripting contract for the `check` command. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the stderr message, and `testWrongVersions` only checks the error text. Neither asserts the process exit code, so a regression such as returning 3 for a disabled feature, or 4 for a version mismatch, would pass. `testFeatureNotEnabled` also covers only the `metadata` subcommand, not `check`. Add `assertEquals(4, ...)` for the disabled case on both subcommands and `assertEquals(3, ...)` for the incompatible-version case.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is reused with a different meaning, and no consumers are updated in this PR
findings.body: Exit code 4 used to mean "recreate upgrade required" and now means "feature disabled". Recreate moves to 3. Any consumer that hardcodes the old value will misread the result. The Operator's update logic, which runs this tool, is one candidate; scripts built on the earlier code are another. A missing feature would then be treated as a recreate signal, and a real recreate (3) as an unknown error. This PR changes no Operator main code, and the Operator tests do not cover the exit-code mapping, because the image-change test never runs the job. Confirm that all consumers use the new 3/4 mapping, ideally via shared constants rather than duplicated literals.
